steps: Lie on your back on the floor with your knees bent and your feet flat. Hook your feet under something sturdy, or have someone hold them down.
Hold one dumbbell against the middle of your chest with both hands, resting your elbows against your sides.
Tighten your stomach and curl your upper body up toward your knees, lifting your shoulders and then your back off the floor.
Sit all the way up, then lower yourself slowly and under control until your back is flat on the floor again.
watchFor: Start with a light weight, or none. Yanking yourself up with a heavy weight strains your lower back.
Don't pull on your neck or let your head snap forward. Keep it in line with your spine.
Keep the movement smooth. If it hurts your lower back, do a smaller movement.

steps: Lie on your back on the floor with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor. Hook your feet under something sturdy or have someone hold them, if you like.
Cross your arms over your chest, or rest your fingertips lightly behind your ears.
Tighten your stomach and curl your upper body up toward your knees, lifting your shoulders and then your back off the floor.
Sit all the way up, then lower yourself slowly back down until your back is flat on the floor.
watchFor: Don't yank on your neck with your hands. Your fingertips just touch your head lightly.
Move smoothly. Don't throw your body up with momentum.
If your lower back hurts, do a smaller movement or lie on a soft mat.

steps: Lie on your back on the floor with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor. Put your fingertips lightly behind your ears, or cross your arms over your chest.
Tighten your stomach muscles.
Lift your head, neck, and shoulders a few inches off the floor by curling your ribs toward your hips. Keep your lower back on the floor.
Squeeze your stomach at the top, then lower slowly.
watchFor: This is a small movement. Don't try to sit all the way up.
Don't pull on your neck with your hands. Keep some space between your chin and chest, like you're holding a small ball there.
Keep your lower back flat on the floor.

steps: Lie on your back with your hands lightly behind your ears. Lift your legs off the floor with your knees bent at a right angle.
Lift your shoulders off the floor and tighten your stomach.
Bring one knee toward your chest while you twist your upper body to bring the opposite elbow toward that knee. At the same time, straighten your other leg out.
Switch sides in a smooth, pedaling motion.
Keep alternating sides.
watchFor: Move slowly, because fast pedaling only uses momentum. Twist from your ribs, not just your elbows.
Don't pull on your neck. Keep your elbows wide.
Keep your lower back pressed toward the floor. If it arches, keep your legs higher.

steps: Lie on your back on the floor with your legs straight and your hands flat on the floor at your sides, or tucked under your hips.
Press your lower back into the floor by tightening your stomach.
Raise both legs together, keeping them straight, until they point straight up at the ceiling.
Lower them slowly toward the floor, stopping before your lower back arches away from the floor.
Raise them again.
watchFor: If your lower back starts to arch off the floor, stop lowering your legs. That's as far as you can go for now.
Bend your knees slightly if straight legs are too hard.
Don't swing your legs. Control them both ways.

steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip (palms facing away from you), hands about shoulder-width apart, arms straight. Let your legs hang straight down.
Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears, and tighten your stomach.
Raise your legs in front of you, keeping them as straight as you can, until they're level with your hips, or higher if you can.
Lower them slowly and stop the swinging before you start the next one.
watchFor: Don't swing your body to get your legs up. Move slowly and stay in control.
You need a solid grip. If your hands tire, stop and rest. Bending your knees makes it easier.
Keep your shoulders active. Don't just hang loose on your joints.

steps: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and your feet flat, or lifted slightly for a harder version.
Lean back slightly, so your body forms a V shape, and keep your back straight, not rounded.
Hold your hands together in front of your chest, or hold a light weight.
Twist your upper body to one side, moving your hands toward the floor next to your hip.
Twist to the other side. Each side counts as one rep. Keep going, side to side.
watchFor: Keep your back straight and don't round it as you lean back. Only lean back as far as your back can stay flat.
Twist from your ribs and shoulders, not by just swinging your arms.
Start with no weight, and move slowly.

steps: Get on your hands and toes with your arms straight, your hands directly under your shoulders, and your body in a straight line from your head to your heels.
Tighten your stomach and keep your hips level.
Bring one knee toward your chest, then switch legs quickly, as if you were running in place with your hands on the floor.
Keep alternating legs at a quick, steady pace for the time you've set.
watchFor: Keep your hips down, in line with your shoulders. Don't let them bounce up.
Keep your wrists flat and directly under your shoulders.
If you feel your back sagging, slow down and keep good form.

steps: Lie on your back with your legs straight and your hands flat under your hips, palms down.
Press your lower back into the floor by tightening your stomach, and lift your legs a few inches off the floor.
Kick your legs up and down in small, quick movements, alternating them, like splashing in water.
Keep kicking for the time you've set.
watchFor: Keep your lower back pressed into the floor. If it arches, raise your legs higher or bend your knees.
Keep your neck relaxed.
Breathe steadily. Don't hold your breath.

steps: Lie on your back on the floor with your legs straight and your arms stretched out above your head.
Tighten your stomach.
At the same time, raise your legs and lift your upper body, reaching your hands toward your toes, so your body folds into a V shape.
Touch your hands to your feet or shins at the top.
Lower back down slowly, with control, until your back and legs are near the floor again.
watchFor: This is a hard movement. Bend your knees, or lift only your legs or only your body at first, if needed.
Don't throw your arms to get momentum, and don't pull on your neck.
If your lower back hurts, stop and try an easier variation.

steps: Get on the floor on your forearms and toes. Place your elbows directly under your shoulders, with your forearms flat and parallel.
Step your feet back so your body forms one long straight line from your head to your heels.
Tighten your stomach and squeeze your buttocks. Keep your neck long and look at the floor a little ahead of your hands.
Hold the position for the time you've set, breathing steadily.
watchFor: Don't let your hips sag toward the floor or poke up into the air. Your body should stay in a straight line.
If your lower back hurts or you can't hold a straight line, lower onto your knees.
Don't hold your breath.

steps: Lie on your side on the floor with your legs straight and your feet stacked. Place your elbow directly under your shoulder, with your forearm flat on the floor.
Push through your forearm and lift your hips off the floor, so your body forms one straight line from your head to your feet.
Tighten your stomach and keep your hips lifted. Rest your other hand on your hip or reach it up to the ceiling.
Hold for the time you've set, breathing steadily, then switch sides.
watchFor: Don't let your hips sag toward the floor or roll forward.
If it's too hard, bend your knees and keep them on the floor.
Keep your shoulder stable and directly over your elbow.

steps: Lie on your back on the floor with your legs straight and your arms stretched out above your head.
Tighten your stomach and press your lower back firmly into the floor.
Lift your legs, your shoulders, and your arms a few inches off the floor, so your body forms a shallow curve like a banana.
Hold that position for the time you've set, breathing steadily.
watchFor: Your lower back must stay pressed into the floor. If it arches up, raise your legs higher or bend your knees.
Keep your neck relaxed and your chin slightly tucked.
Stop if your back hurts, and try a version with your knees bent.

steps: Lie on your back on the floor. Lift your arms straight up above your chest, and lift your legs so your knees are bent at a right angle, with your shins parallel to the floor.
Tighten your stomach and press your lower back into the floor.
Slowly lower one arm behind your head and straighten the opposite leg out in front of you, both hovering just above the floor.
Bring them back to the start and switch to the other arm and leg.
Keep alternating, moving slowly.
watchFor: Your lower back must stay pressed into the floor. If it arches, make the movement smaller.
Move slowly. Speed makes it easier and takes away the point.
Breathe steadily.

steps: Get on your hands and knees on the floor, with your hands under your shoulders and your knees under your hips.
Keep your back flat and your neck long, looking at the floor.
Slowly reach one arm straight forward and the opposite leg straight back, until both are in line with your body.
Hold for a moment without letting your hips tilt or your back sag.
Bring them back, then switch to the other arm and leg.
watchFor: Keep your hips level, as if there were a glass of water on your lower back.
Don't lift your leg higher than your hips, which would arch your back.
Move slowly and stay steady.

steps: Set a cable to the highest position and attach a handle. Stand sideways to the machine with your feet a little wider than your shoulders.
Hold the handle with both hands, arms straight, above the shoulder nearest the machine.
Pull the handle down and across your body in a diagonal line toward the opposite hip, twisting your torso as you go. Let your back foot turn naturally.
Pause, then slowly bring the handle back up along the same path.
Finish all your reps, then switch sides.
watchFor: Twist from your middle, not by swinging your arms. Keep your arms mostly straight.
Use a light weight so you can control the twist. Don't jerk.
Keep your knees slightly bent and your back straight.

steps: Set a cable to the highest position and attach a rope. Kneel on the floor facing the machine, a step back from it.
Hold the rope by your head, with your hands beside your ears.
Tighten your stomach and curl your body down, bringing your elbows toward your knees and rounding your upper back.
Squeeze your stomach at the bottom, then slowly come back up.
watchFor: The movement comes from your stomach curling, not from your hips or arms. Keep your hips still.
Don't pull with your arms or sit back on your heels.
Use a weight you can control and don't jerk.

steps: Sit in the machine and adjust the seat so the pads rest lightly against your chest or shoulders, depending on its design. Put your feet under the roller pads if there are any.
Hold the handles and sit up straight.
Tighten your stomach and curl your upper body forward, bringing your ribs toward your hips.
Squeeze at the bottom, then slowly return to the start.
watchFor: Move slowly and use your stomach, not your arms or your hip muscles, to pull the weight.
Don't let the weight stack slam.
Keep your neck relaxed and your head in line with your spine.
